description:
Optimize measured bit transpose and bitslice conversion costs, including the layout conversion that production BCH encoding pays.

## Background

The library uses a 64x64 AVX2 mask/shift/XOR transpose and retains a PSHUFB alternative. A 32x8 movemask/byte-shift candidate has different input geometry; comparisons must include tile assembly and packing. Existing BCH performance receipts and adapters provide the production evidence context.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Satisfy the [Zen 3 measurement contract](dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md) for correctness, reproducible release benchmarks, comparison validity and adoption; receipts pin its committed version, the frozen protocol and the cell addendum. Include mandatory before/after evidence for production changes and preserve negative outcomes.

- [hard] REQ-07: Compare the existing 64x64 transpose, its PSHUFB alternative and movemask-based candidates against M4RI and Bitshuffle only after defining an equivalent bit mapping and including adapter costs. Freeze exact tile shapes, tails and matrix dimensions in the experiment protocol.

- [hard] REQ-08: Preserve the canonical relation $\mathrm{output}[c][r] = \mathrm{input}[r][c]$ under little-endian bit indexing, including zero-sized matrices, non-square matrices, unaligned storage and partial boundary tiles. Run shared transpose and bitslice round-trip contracts.

- [hard] REQ-09: Measure isolated transform latency, bulk throughput, packing/unpacking and the current BCH conversion/encoding consumer using the established harness. Capture the pinned current pre-change implementation under the shared protocol; historical pre-cutover receipts are context only. Generic transform feasibility does not require completion of the independent BCH scorecard campaign.

- [hard] REQ-10: Attribute scratch-buffer traffic versus actual compiler spills in release assembly and profiles. Select any measured improvements through the shared transpose/bitslice abstraction and reject candidates whose complete conversion cost fails the frozen rule.
title: Optimize bit transpose and bitslice conversion
